There are several issues in the tokenization.py file that cause word processing to fail. The most noticeable problems are:

1. The collocation scoring function has incorrect sign in the log function


entries.content: I fixed six defects in `wordcloud/tokenization.py`: (1) the binomial log-likelihood helper `l` used `-` instead of `+` between its terms, and (2) `score` swapped `count1`/`count2` (scrambling the Dunning likelihood-ratio probabilities) and returned `2 * score` instead of `-2 * score`, so collocation scores were always ≤ 0 and never reached the threshold; (3) the bigram loop had `word1`/`word2` swapped when looking up standard forms; (4) plural merging created `word[:-1] + 'e'` instead of `word[:-1]`, and (5) the plural standard-case mapping used `singular.upper()` (causing the reported `KeyError`); (6) case selection used `min` instead of `max`, picking the least frequent capitalization. Additionally, bigrams containing stopwords are now skipped in the collocation loop (they aren't in the unigram counts and must not become collocations, per `test_collocation_stopwords`), and the `score` guard was tightened to `<=` returning 0 to avoid a division-by-zero when a word fills the whole document. All 76 existing tests pass, and extra checks confirm collocations are detected, plurals merge correctly, and the most frequent case is preserved.
